correctness.rationale: A complete partition into \(A(S)\) and \(B(w)\) normal forms covers every ideal. The minimal-complement rule gives three case-exact transitions, and their disjoint two-, three-, and eight-cycle decomposition accounts for every ideal. The eight-cycle contains two distinct A-states and six distinct B-states; distinct complement-pairs cannot coincide. Three-symbol words give exact 3-cycles by free coordinatewise rotation. An independent direct-bitmask exhaustive verifier enumerated every ideal and cycle at \(1\le n\le8\); cycle weighted count equals \(2^n+3^n\) algebraically for all n. \(n\ge2\) guarantees at least one 8-cycle; proof is not inferred from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The primary 2014/2016 full texts establish a general period algorithm for skeletal posets and a universal level three-cycle, but their stated results and inspected sections do not supply the length-by-length orbit multiplicities proved here. The 2022 rooted-tree results assume a unique minimal element, absent in both orientations of this poset for \(n\ge2\). Targeted semantic, exact-expression, and graph-incidence literature searches located no exact equivalent cycle distribution. The known cardinality sequence does not imply orbit structure. Residual risk remains for unindexed computations or stronger undiscovered statements; this is a self-review best-knowledge assessment, not a guarantee of worldwide novelty.
residual_risks: A specialized non-indexed computation may have stated the same orbit-type formulas; internet and semantic search cannot establish exhaustive uniqueness.

General forest rowmotion constructions may permit recovering this special case by an unpublished or uninspected specialized application, although inspected period-only results do not directly imply it.

value.rationale: The star graph-incidence construction is a canonical graph-to-poset family with exponentially many ideals and a tree Hasse diagram of mixed orientation, outside rooted-tree tiling hypotheses. Full closed-form orbit multiplicities (including all nonlevel cycles) substantially refine general finite-period results and expose why \(\operatorname{lcm}(2,3,8)=24\) arises; cycle counts are natural dynamic invariants rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The exact infinite-family classification is self-contained and may serve as an explicit test case for mixed-orientation tree rowmotion.
